Market today: The market mood is cautious, with a headline warning of a potential 15% S&P 500 correction. While some tech M&A is happening, Netflix's post-earnings drop on guidance shows investors are quick to punish any weakness in growth names, which is key for your tech/chip heavy book.

Your holdings: SOXL is a major concern, down -56.6% with a blown stop. MUU (-32.11%), SPAL (-36.26%), and SMCI (-26%) are also "SELL" status with significant losses and stops that have been breached. Remember, margin amplifies these drops.

Watch: Keep a close eye on overall market sentiment, especially any signs of the predicted S&P 500 correction. Also, monitor how other tech names react to earnings or guidance, as Netflix's drop could be a canary in the coal mine.

Bottom line: With significant drawdowns in leveraged positions and a market correction warning, risk management is paramount right now.
plays: Your stops are blown on SOXL, MUU, SPAL, and SMCI with heavy losses. Re-evaluate these "SELL" positions immediately to prevent further capital erosion.
Consider a hedge: Given the S&P 500 correction warning, look at TECS (entry 60.07-60.01, stop 59.64) as a short-term inverse tech play.
Manage SMH: Respect the "TRIM" status on SMH at 546.36, with a stop at 540.
